\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Finite Noise Optimization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Sharp.FiniteNoiseOptimization
\section{Overview}
Optimization on a weighted moment sphere produces nonnegative extremizers. Differentiation and strict concavity show that these extremizers have at most two distinct coordinate values.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Compactness of a weighted moment sphere]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_moment_sphere_compact}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$ for every $i$, and $p>0$. The set $\{f\in\bbr^I:\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p=1\}$ is compact in the usual finite-dimensional topology.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of a nonnegative noise maximizer]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.exists_nonnegative_noise_maximizer}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_moment_sphere_compact}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, $1<p<2$, and $0\le\rho\le1$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. There exists a nonnegative vector $g$ with $G(g)=1$ and $F(f)\le F(g)$ whenever $G(f)=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A strict-concavity level has two values]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_concave_level_two_values}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be finite, let $\varphi:\bbr\to\bbr$ be strictly concave on $[0,\infty)$, and let $f:I\to[0,\infty)$ satisfy $\varphi(f_i)=c$ for every $i$ and some $c\in\bbr$. There exist $a,b\ge0$ such that every $f_i$ equals $a$ or $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of weighted moment and noise forms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_homogeneity}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, $w:I\to\bbr$, and $p,\rho,t\in\bbr$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. Then $G(tf)=|t|^pG(f)$ and $F(tf)=t^2F(f)$ for every real vector $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative at a quotient maximum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.derivative_eq_mul_of_isLocalMax_quotient}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $f,g:\bbr\to\bbr$ be differentiable at $x$, with $f^{\prime}(x)=a$, $g^{\prime}(x)=b$, and $g(x)=1$. If $t\mapsto f(t)/g(t)^r$ has a local maximum at $x$ for $r\in\bbr$, then $a=rf(x)b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Normalizing weighted moment and noise forms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_normalization}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_homogeneity}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, $w:I\to\bbr$, $p\ne0$, and $\rho\in\bbr$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. If $G(f)>0$ and $c=G(f)^{-1/p}$, then $G(cf)=1$ and $F(cf)=F(f)/G(f)^{2/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Directional derivatives of weighted noise forms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_directional_derivatives}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be finite, $w:I\to\bbr$, $p>1$, $\rho\in\bbr$, $g_i\ge0$, and $h\in\bbr^I$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. At $t=0$, the derivative of $G(g+th)$ is $p\sum_iw_ig_i^{p-1}h_i$, and that of $F(g+th)$ is $2[\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_ih_i+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_ig_i)(\sum_iw_ih_i)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stationarity of a normalized noise maximizer]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_stationarity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.derivative_eq_mul_of_isLocalMax_quotient, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_directional_derivatives, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_normalization}
\difficulty{6}
Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, $1<p<2$, and $0\le\rho<1$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. If $g_i\ge0$, $G(g)=1$, and $F(f)\le F(g)$ whenever $G(f)=1$, then $F(g)\ge1$ and $F(g)g_i^{p-1}-\rho^2g_i=(1-\rho^2)\sum_jw_jg_j$ for every $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise maximizers take at most two values]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_two_values}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_concave_level_two_values, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_stationarity}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, $1<p<2$, and $0\le\rho<1$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. If $g_i\ge0$, $G(g)=1$, and $F(f)\le F(g)$ whenever $G(f)=1$, then some $a,b\ge0$ satisfy $g_i\in\{a,b\}$ for every $i$.
\end{theorem}
